newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM nearby platinum jumps as spot prices surge.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM nearby platinum jumps as spot prices surge.

text.p: Nearby contracts of yen-based Tokyo platinum futures ended sharply higher on Friday, as spot platinum prices rocketed on panic buying, traders said.

"Funds are shifting attention to the platinum market from the palladium market in an attempt to squeeze the market. There was panic buying in the spot market both by Japanese traders and overseas players," one trader said.
TOCOM spot June, which has no daily price limit, vaulted by 76 yen per gram to end at 1,660 yen. July surged by its daily limit of 50 yen before closing 21 yen higher at 1,530 yen.
Benchmark April was seven higher at 1,384 yen.
Higher spot market prices relative to TOCOM futures prices have made arbitrage trade between TOCOM and the spot market uneconomical, the trader said.
Spot platinum was quoted at $480.00/510.00 per ounce at 0714 GMT, its highest level since 1990, compared with $430.00/440.00 in London on Thursday.
A protracted delay in Russian sales and an attempt to squeeze the market were behind the surge, traders said.
Ongoing PGM supply talks for 1997 will continue into next week, traders said. They said the market would remain nervous until Russian supplies start flowing into the market.
Palladium futures were mostly higher following rising spot palladium prices. Spot June was 24 yen higher at 768 yen.
Benchmark April finished unchanged at 565 yen.
Gold and silver futures ended slightly higher in tandem with firmer bullion. Benchmark April gold closed up eight yen at 1,271 yen.
In the spot market, bullion was quoted at $344.50/345.00 at 0737 GMT, against $343.10/60 in New York on Thursday.
Benchmark April silver was up 2.2 yen at 179.4 yen.
